faq_caffeinate_question: Does caffeinate or Amphetamine not do this already?
faq_caffeinate_answer: They keep your Mac awake until a set time or until you stop them. They do not know when an agent works. Agent Caffeine does, also with the lid closed on battery, and lets your Mac sleep after.
faq_battery_question: Does it drain my battery when nothing runs?
faq_battery_answer: No. When no agent works, your Mac sleeps as usual. On battery, Agent Caffeine also stops at {floor}%.
faq_admin_answer: Only to stay awake with the lid closed on battery. You allow a small helper once in System Settings. Everything else works without it.
faq_detection_question: How does it know that an agent is working?

faq_phone_question: Can I reach my agent from my phone while the lid is closed?
faq_phone_answer: Yes. Choose Stay reachable, and your Mac stays awake for 1, 2 or 4 hours. On battery with the lid closed it needs the helper. A message cannot wake a sleeping Mac.

compare_price_heading: What you get for the price
compare_price_text_launch: Agent Caffeine costs {price} once for up to {macs} Macs at the launch price, then {full}, after a 7-day free trial. Two other tools on this page are free, and one has a free plan for the lid open. Many of them also keep a Mac awake with the lid closed on battery, read the hooks of an agent, or stop for a low battery or heat.
compare_price_text: Agent Caffeine costs {price} once for up to {macs} Macs, after a 7-day free trial. Two other tools on this page are free, and one has a free plan for the lid open. Many of them also keep a Mac awake with the lid closed on battery, read the hooks of an agent, or stop for a low battery or heat.
compare_together: What we put together in one app: the state of each agent, also when it waits for you, the closed lid on battery, a stop at a low battery, a stop for heat, and a notification when an agent needs you or finishes. As far as the pages of the other tools say, none of them states all of these. Their pages can be silent about a thing the tool does, so read their pages too.
compare_adrafinil_1: Adrafinil is free and open source (MIT). One installer sets up hooks for 9 agents: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Aider, Hermes, OpenCode, Cline and Pi. It keeps the Mac awake with the lid closed only while an agent works, and it stops when the Mac gets too hot under a closed lid. Its release notes also name a battery cutout, with no level.
compare_adrafinil_2: An agent can ask it for more time after its answer, through an MCP tool or a command, for example for a long build. Agent Caffeine has a command and an MCP server for this too. Adrafinil has one thing we do not have: it gives you the lines to add an agent of your own.
compare_adrafinil_3: For Claude Code it also knows when a session waits for you. A setting decides what happens then: the Mac stays awake, sleeps after a grace period, or sleeps at once. The menu shows what the session waits for.
compare_adrafinil_4: If you want a free tool and your agent is on that list, Adrafinil does the job. It needs macOS 26.4 or later. Its pages state a chime when you close the lid while it keeps the Mac awake, as Agent Caffeine has, and a summary when you open the lid. They do not state a notification when an agent finishes.
compare_holdmylid_1: Hold My Lid costs $9.99 once for up to 3 Macs, and has a free trial. Its page calls $9.99 an early price and names $14.99 as the normal one. Its page gives two lists of the agents whose lifecycle hooks it reads. The answer in its FAQ names 3: Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode. The grid "Works out of the box" marks 7: those 3 and Gemini, Pi, Copilot CLI and Hermes. For others, such as Cursor, it checks the process. It runs on macOS 14 or later, on Apple silicon and Intel.
compare_holdmylid_2: It stops at a battery level you set, it has a mode that works only when the Mac is plugged in, and it sends a notification when your agents finish.
compare_holdmylid_3: If you want a mode that works only while the Mac is plugged in, pick Hold My Lid. Its pages do not state a stop for heat, a state for an agent that waits for you, or whether the closed lid on battery needs a helper.
compare_lidrun_1: LidRun has a free plan that keeps the Mac awake with the lid open, with timers, a mode for charging only and a stop at a low battery. The closed lid and Auto Mode are in the paid plan, after a limited number of free closed-lid runs: $9.90 once for 1 Mac, $19.90 for 3 Macs, with a refund within 14 days.
compare_lidrun_2: Auto Mode watches the processes of Claude Code, Cursor, Docker and Ollama. LidRun also has webhooks, it can run a command and let the Mac sleep when the command ends, and it keeps a log that says why a session started and stopped. It runs on macOS 13 or later, on Apple silicon and Intel.
compare_lidrun_3: If you also leave Docker builds or local models running, or you want webhooks, pick LidRun. If the lid stays open, its free plan may be all you need. Its pages do not state that it reads the state an agent reports about itself.
compare_clamshell_1: Clamshell keeps a MacBook awake with the lid closed, on power or on battery, with no admin rights, no helper and no sudo. No other tool on this page states that, and ours needs a helper for battery. It costs $9.99 once for 1 Mac or $19.99 for 3 Macs after a 7-day free trial, with a refund within 14 days.
compare_clamshell_2: Its page says that it does not detect agents. You arm it yourself: hold Option and close the lid. A script can also arm and disarm it. The stop for heat is always on, and the stop at a low battery is there when you turn it on.
compare_clamshell_3: If you do not want to give a tool admin rights, or you want to decide yourself when the Mac stays awake, pick Clamshell. It runs only on Apple silicon laptops with macOS 14 or later.
compare_amphetamine_1: Amphetamine is free on the Mac App Store, with no in-app purchases. It is a keep-awake tool for general use, with many triggers: an app that runs, a Wi-Fi network, a display or a drive that is connected, the charger, processor use.
compare_amphetamine_2: It can keep a MacBook awake with the lid closed, and it can end a session when the battery is low. Its listing names no AI coding agents. The nearest trigger keeps the Mac awake while an app you pick is running. The latest version on the listing is 5.3.2, from November 10, 2023.
compare_amphetamine_3: If you want a free tool for more than agents, such as downloads, a presentation or a Mac that must stay awake on one network, pick Amphetamine. We wrote more about it in [our guide to Amphetamine](/blog/amphetamine-mac).
compare_caffeinate_text: `caffeinate` comes with macOS and is free. It keeps the Mac awake until a time you give or until a process ends. Its manual says that the option that prevents system sleep is valid only on AC power, and it lists no option for agents, the battery level or heat ([a copy of the manual](https://ss64.com/mac/caffeinate.html)). If one command in one terminal is all you run, it may be enough. We wrote more in [our guide to caffeinate](/blog/caffeinate-mac).

privacy_meta_description: What Agent Caffeine, its purchase and this website collect: no telemetry in the app, Polar for payments, self-hosted analytics with no cookies.
privacy_intro: Agent Caffeine is made and sold by me, Mert Duzgun, an individual based in Antalya, Türkiye. I am responsible for the data on this page. Here is what the app, a purchase and this website collect, and why.
privacy_app_reads: The app has no telemetry, no analytics and no account. To see whether an agent is working, it reads the list of running processes on your Mac, the state and session files that Claude Code and Codex keep in `~/.claude` and `~/.codex`, and the times at which other agents write their session files. From those files it takes only the state of a session (working, waiting for you or idle), its folder and its name, and shows them in the menu. For Cursor it reads the transcript files in `~/.cursor/projects`. From those it takes only where a turn starts and ends and the time the file was last written, never the text. It also reads the battery level and the lid angle of your Mac, to let it sleep when the battery is low and to dim the display as the lid closes. None of that leaves your Mac.
privacy_app_detection: Better detection is off until you switch it on for an agent. Agent Caffeine then adds a few lines to that agent's own settings file and keeps a backup next to it. The agent writes its state to a small file in Agent Caffeine's folder on your Mac. That file holds the state and the name of the event, and nothing you or the agent typed. When you switch better detection off, Agent Caffeine removes its lines again.
privacy_app_requests: It makes two kinds of network request:
privacy_app_updates: Updates. About once a day it asks caffeinagent.com for the update feed, and when you agree to an update it downloads it from there. These requests carry what every download request carries, such as your IP address and a user agent with the app's name and version. They carry nothing that identifies you.
privacy_app_license: License. When you enter a key, the app sends it to Polar with your Mac's model (for example "MacBookPro18,3"), never the computer's name. Polar answers with an activation id. About once a day the app sends the key and that activation id to check that the key is still good, and it sends them once more when you deactivate the Mac. During the free trial the app sends nothing to Polar.
privacy_buying_polar: Payments go through [Polar](https://polar.sh), the merchant of record: Polar collects the payment, handles tax and sends the invoice. At checkout Polar collects your email address, name, billing country and payment details.
privacy_buying_received: From Polar I receive your email address, name, country and what you bought. I use them to send your license key and to answer support. I never see your card number.
privacy_site_analytics: I count page views and clicks on this site with OpenPanel, an analytics tool I run on my own server at analytics.vinena.studio. It also records how the page is used: pointer movement, scrolling and clicks. I watch these recordings to find where the page is unclear and to improve it. A recording shows only this site, never the rest of your screen, and anything typed into a field is hidden. The requests go through this site first, at `/api/op`, and carry your IP address and your browser's user agent. There are no cookies. The app itself sends none of this.
privacy_site_download: When you download the app, the site also counts the download on the server, with no cookie: the version, where on the page the button was, the source of the link that brought you here, and the country and the kind of browser, taken from your IP address and user agent.
privacy_site_source: If the link that brought you here names its source (for example `utm_source`), your browser keeps that source until you close the tab. The page view and the download count carry it, and the checkout link passes it to Polar, so I can see which link led to a download or an order.
privacy_site_theme: If you pick a light or dark theme, the choice is kept in your browser's local storage. It never leaves your browser.
privacy_site_hosts: Vercel serves this site, and Cloudflare sits in front of it and stores the app downloads. Both see the IP address of each request, as any host does.
privacy_email: If you write to me, I keep the conversation so I can answer you.

privacy_rights: I keep purchase records for as long as the law requires for bookkeeping. You can ask me to see, correct or delete what I hold about you. I do not sell your data, and I do not share it beyond the services named on this page.
